punchline: Marcus Aurelius, emperor of Rome, wrote himself a note to argue his way out of a warm bed.
thirty_sec: Marcus Aurelius wrote what we call Meditations in Greek, on campaign, just for himself. In one note he's lying in bed telling himself he's getting up to do a human being's work, then asking whether he was made to stay under the covers. In another he starts the day expecting busybodies and ungrateful people, and reminds himself not to be angry. It was probably never meant to be published.
